steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: follow the trust chain
steps.detail: A token is a signed claim, not a database account and not proof that every requested operation is allowed. Start with services/auth-service/src/main/java/in/craves/auth/web/AuthController.java. The controller exposes /api/v1/auth/firebase/exchange, /refresh, /logout and /me. It delegates exchange and lifecycle work to AuthService. The /me method refuses a missing Authentication or a principal that is not the Auth service's CurrentUser. Trace the JWT filter into that principal before reading any controller. In the filter, distinguish decoding claims from verifying the signature and establishing the request identity. Then trace live account/session checks in the service. Write the sequence as Firebase proof, Craves exchange, Craves access credential, verified principal, operation permission and owned data. These are separate responsibilities. A customer session on a staff member's device must not silently become an administrator session. Do not infer deployed provider settings or current role grants from a source snapshot.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: authentication versus ownership
steps.detail: Investigate a rejected request from outside inward: was the same-origin web request sent, did the BFF forward the intended session, did the gateway route it correctly, did Java recognize the principal, and did the operation permit that principal? Record the method, path, status, timestamp and sanitized correlation identifier at each boundary. Do not copy Authorization headers, OTPs, refresh tokens or Firebase credentials into a ticket. A 401 and a forbidden owner/role response are not interchangeable symptoms. A successful /me response does not authorize reading another customer's order. Equally, a temporary upstream failure is not proof that the user must be permanently signed out. Use the existing error contract rather than replacing every failure with an empty success.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: construct a trust-boundary evidence table
steps.detail: In a local clone, run mvn -B -ntp -f services/auth-service/pom.xml -Dtest=AdminSessionPolicyTest,ConsumerSessionRegressionTest test. Read the actual test methods, not only their green summary. Create five synthetic cases: absent principal, ordinary consumer roles, known internal role in a valid admin family, expired signed access credential, and changed account authorization. For each, identify which layer rejects it and which later layer must never execute. Write the expected assertion before changing a fixture. In a disposable training branch, deliberately replace an internal role with CUSTOMER and prove that the negative test catches the attempted privilege change. Restore the fixture and rerun. Deliver the test output, exact source revision and a diagram in plain text; do not use real accounts or contact an OTP provider.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: explain the difference between Firebase proof, a Craves access token, CurrentUser and resource ownership without consulting the answer key. Demonstrate one negative test that fails when its protection is deliberately removed in a training branch. Passing the two reading questions alone does not demonstrate this skill.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: read permissions as explicit contracts
steps.detail: InternalAdminRoles.java defines nine named roles: PLATFORM_ADMIN, SUPPORT_ADMIN, PAYMENTS_ADMIN, OPERATIONS_ADMIN, CHEF_ADMIN, COMPLIANCE_ADMIN, SUBSCRIPTION_ADMIN, NOTIFICATION_ADMIN and AUDIT_ADMIN. A role's description is an orientation aid; the endpoint's actual authorization code is the executable boundary. For Academy, compare requireAdmin, requireManager and requireReporter in AcademyController. Learners and source readers are broader than private-plan editors; audited team-report access has its own boundary. Follow the verified server principal into those checks. Never accept a role submitted by the browser as authoritative. Notice normalization and null handling: strings with spaces and case differences are not a reason to create an additional role, while a generic ADMIN label is not one of the nine recognized codes.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: hiding a button is insufficient
steps.detail: Suppose the screen hides the plan editor from SUPPORT_ADMIN. A caller can still submit the HTTP request directly, so the Java endpoint must reject it independently of the UI and BFF. Test both the exact intended role and a nearby but wrong internal role. A test that only excludes anonymous callers misses horizontal privilege problems between administrators. Build a matrix with operation rows and role columns, including a nonstaff consumer and a malformed claim. In the expected cells, state permit or deny and whether an audit entry is required. Keep the matrix tied to a source revision and the endpoint implementation; do not claim that it is the live directory of people holding those roles.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: add a least-privilege regression
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -ntp -f services/auth-service/pom.xml -Dtest=AcademyCoreTest,InternalAdminRolesTest test. Open everyExplicitInternalAdminCanLearnButCustomersCannot and roleBoundariesAndMalformedClaimsFailClosed. In a local training copy, add a test showing that AUDIT_ADMIN can use the reporting guard but cannot use the plan-management guard. Use the existing actor helper and a random synthetic identity, not a manually minted production token. Verify the exception status and ensure a rejected operation cannot invoke its persistence dependency. Extend the matrix to the source-reading route. A reviewer should be able to point from each matrix cell to an assertion. This is authorization testing, not permission provisioning: no role grant, IAM change or production account mutation belongs in the exercise.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: submit the operation-by-role matrix, the new test and its passing run. Explain why an administrator's business title does not automatically imply PLATFORM_ADMIN, and why a hidden menu is not an access control.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: understand rotating admin sessions
steps.detail: Read AdminSessionService.java beside AdminSessionPolicyTest.java. The reviewed implementation distinguishes a short-lived access credential from a longer administrator session family. The family has an original authentication boundary; obtaining a replacement token does not begin a new unlimited administrator day. Trace refresh input validation, family lookup, account and role validation, rotation and response construction. Follow the receipt used to reconcile an ambiguous refresh attempt. Identify which information is stored as a digest and which values are returned only to the legitimate caller. Look for database locking and transaction boundaries before explaining race behavior. A Java synchronized block would only coordinate one process; persisted coordination is the relevant property when requests can reach different processes or when a process restarts.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: retry is not replay permission
steps.detail: Draw two timelines. In the first, the browser sends a refresh, the server commits, and the response is lost. The same logical attempt must be distinguishable from a new attempt reusing an old credential. In the second, logout races with refresh. Determine what makes the replacement unusable after logout instead of assuming request arrival order. Consult AdminSessionPersistenceTest for actual database cases before making any claim about all races. Also separate a controlled-clock test of an eight-hour boundary from an eight-hour observation in a real browser. Both are useful evidence, but they answer different questions. Never disable live revocation or extend the absolute deadline simply to make a troublesome client appear stable.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: annotate a complete request
steps.detail: Choose one synthetic refresh case and produce an annotated path covering AuthController.refresh, AuthService's refresh decision, AdminSessionService, the owned persistence record and the returned token policy. For every step, name its inputs, trust assumptions, database effects and failure response. Run AdminSessionPolicyTest locally first. Database session tests require their own explicitly documented disposable database settings; inspect the class annotation and setup before running them. Never aim a test suite that drops schemas at an existing environment. Review the source test for simultaneous logout and refresh and describe what assertion proves the survivor is unusable. A diagram that stops at the controller is incomplete; a diagram that copies secret values is unacceptable.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: one request sequence, two race timelines, and the exact names of the policy and persistence tests supporting each conclusion. Mark database execution NOT RUN when its disposable setup was not created; do not turn a skipped test into a pass.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: design a harmless protected extension
steps.detail: Training-only feature brief: add an administrator-only, read-only learning-summary response inside the Academy module. It may expose existing learning totals for the current verified learner, but it must not accept an arbitrary identity or alter account/session behavior. Start with AcademyController's existing principal and role guards and AcademyService.state; avoid inventing a new login mechanism. List the controller contract, response shape, service method, tests and thin web adapter that would change. Reuse existing learning facts instead of adding a table for a derived value. Do not expose the internal database entity or a second learner's progress. Keep the response private and uncached. This is a local capstone specification, not approval to add the feature to Craves production.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: specify the contract before the form
steps.detail: Write acceptance cases for an authorized learner, anonymous caller, customer, another internal role, empty learning history and a transient dependency failure. The actor must come from the verified principal in all cases; a query parameter or JSON identity is not a shortcut. Decide whether an existing route can return the information without expanding the attack surface. For a genuinely new route, include its BFF allowlist and gateway exposure in the plan, but do not run a provisioning script during training. An accurate plan explicitly distinguishes a route that exists at the pinned revision from a proposed route. Add a response-shape assertion that would catch accidental inclusion of tokens, email addresses, private plans or raw database rows.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: implement and defend the vertical slice locally
steps.detail: Create a local branch named training/academy-learning-summary. Implement the smallest read-only Java extension using the established Academy controller/service pattern, and add success, denial and response-privacy tests next to AcademyCoreTest. Where a service query is needed, use the existing learner-scoped state operation rather than writing an unrestricted select. Add a thin client parser and render loading, empty, success, denied and temporary-failure states in a training-only screen. Run the Java tests plus the existing Academy web policy tests and typecheck. Your submission must contain full file contents, an API example with synthetic data, test output and a rollback explanation. Do not merge, deploy, modify IAM, change global authentication or call customer/provider APIs.

lessons.lab: Peer review checks the server-derived actor, explicit role guard, learner isolation, runtime response validation and unchanged login/logout behavior. The reviewer should reject an implementation that only secures the browser button or claims readiness without running the negative cases.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: release Auth without treating it as disposable
steps.detail: Academy shares the Auth process, so even a learning-content change has a login-service deployment boundary. Separate course validation from production promotion. First verify JSON structure, source provenance, Academy tests and ordinary session regressions. Then record the exact reviewed source, current healthy Auth image, revision, configuration fingerprints, migration state and backup evidence. The repository contains azure-pipelines-auth-service.yml and scripts/release/deploy-single-service-preserve-runtime.sh for an Auth-only image update. Read them before selecting a pipeline. Do not use a seven-service release for a narrowly scoped Academy change unless a separately approved dependency actually requires it. Preserve the existing one-replica configuration and currently enabled capabilities; do not recreate secret references from memory.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: avoid destructive recovery
steps.detail: If the new catalog fails validation during startup, stop promotion and diagnose the exact resource file in a nonproduction build. Do not make the validator permissive just to start the process. If a deployed Auth revision is unhealthy, use the established previous-image rollback path and retain all learning and session data. A content rollback does not require deleting academy_schema or editing Flyway checksums. Test access boundaries after recovery, because a healthy process does not prove that a routed administrator request succeeds. A content-only reading expansion can retain existing quiz IDs and assessment version; changing questions or grading semantics requires an explicit progress/version policy rather than silently resetting learners.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: prepare a verifiable release packet
steps.detail: Run python3 scripts/academy/verify-curriculum.py --git in a complete Git clone. Run mvn -B -ntp -f services/auth-service/pom.xml -Dtest=AcademyCoreTest,AdminSessionPolicyTest,ConsumerSessionRegressionTest test. For AcademyPersistenceTest, use only its explicitly named disposable craves_academy_ci database as documented. Fill a release sheet with source SHA, all executed/skipped test counts, artifact digest, previous revision, one-replica readback, unchanged configuration proof and authorized catalog/quiz smoke evidence. Leave live fields pending until observed. Include checks that a second learner is unchanged and that retrying a successful quiz receipt adds no XP. The exercise ends with a simulated rollback decision; no Azure update, OTP, payment or delivery is executed.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a release packet that another engineer can audit without guessing which build or environment was tested. A reviewer must be able to distinguish source publication, successful CI, image deployment and authenticated production acceptance.
